content.overview: A company must notify the Registrar in the prescribed form of full payment or satisfaction of a registered charge within thirty days. On application by the company or charge-holder, the Registrar may allow intimation within three hundred days on prescribed additional fees. The Registrar ordinarily notifies the charge-holder to show cause within a period not exceeding fourteen days before recording satisfaction, except where the intimation is in the specified form and signed by the charge-holder.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 82 (Company to report satisfaction of charge). A company must notify the Registrar, in the prescribed form, of payment or satisfaction in full of a registered charge within thirty days of payment or satisfaction. On application by the company or charge-holder, the Registrar may allow the intimation to be made within three hundred days on payment of prescribed additional fees. On receipt, the Registrar ordinarily sends the charge-holder a notice to show cause within a period not exceeding fourteen days why satisfaction should not be recorded. If no cause is shown, the Registrar orders a memorandum of satisfaction to be entered in the register of charges and informs the company. If cause is shown, the Registrar records a note and informs the company. The show-cause notice is not required where the intimation is in the specified form and signed by the charge-holder. Section 82 does not limit the Registrar's separate power under section 83 to enter satisfaction/release on satisfactory evidence without company intimation. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Company intimation and deadline
sections.body: The company must give the Registrar prescribed-form intimation of full payment or satisfaction of a registered charge within thirty days of the payment or satisfaction.

sections.heading: Extension to three hundred days
sections.body: On application by the company or charge-holder, the Registrar may allow the intimation within three hundred days of payment or satisfaction on payment of prescribed additional fees.

sections.heading: Charge-holder notice and satisfaction entry
sections.body: On receipt of the intimation, the Registrar ordinarily sends the charge-holder a notice requiring cause to be shown within a period not exceeding fourteen days. If no cause is shown, the Registrar orders a memorandum of satisfaction to be entered in the register of charges and informs the company.

sections.heading: Cause shown or signed charge-holder intimation
sections.body: If cause is shown, the Registrar records a note and informs the company. The show-cause notice is not required where the intimation is in the specified form and signed by the charge-holder.

sections.heading: Section 83 preserved
sections.body: Section 82 does not affect the Registrar's power under section 83 to enter a satisfaction/release memorandum on satisfactory evidence even without company intimation.

hypotheticals.question: A registered charge is fully paid, and the company wants to notify the Registrar after thirty days. What does section 82 permit?
hypotheticals.analysis: The ordinary period is thirty days. On application by the company or charge-holder, the Registrar may allow intimation within three hundred days on payment of prescribed additional fees.

hypotheticals.question: The charge-holder signs the prescribed satisfaction intimation. Must the Registrar still issue the show-cause notice?
hypotheticals.analysis: The proviso states that the show-cause notice is not required where the intimation is in the specified form and signed by the charge-holder.

distinctions.title: Company intimation and Registrar's independent entry power
distinctions.left: Section 82 requires company intimation of full satisfaction and provides the charge-holder notice process.
distinctions.right: Section 83 permits the Registrar to enter satisfaction/release on satisfactory evidence without company intimation.

rows.left: Thirty days; possible extension to 300 days; charge-holder notice unless exception applies
rows.right: Registrar informs affected parties within thirty days after making entry

misconceptions.trap: Treating the thirty-day period as incapable of extension.
misconceptions.correction: The Registrar may, on application by the company or charge-holder, allow intimation within three hundred days on additional fees.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the Registrar always records satisfaction immediately after company intimation.
misconceptions.correction: The ordinary process includes notice to the charge-holder and an opportunity to show cause, subject to the signed-charge-holder-intimation proviso.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 82 as the only route for recording satisfaction or release.
misconceptions.correction: Section 83 separately permits the Registrar to make entries on satisfactory evidence even without company intimation.
